assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity that hijacks E3 ligases to degrade proteins turned 'undruggable' targets into tractable ones. It supplies a general molecular design principle (bifunctional recognition and induced assembly) and has changed what chemists and clinicians can do, with degraders now in late-stage clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies delivered the PROTAC concept and its first demonstrations. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular-glue degraders and underpins the clinical IMiD story. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others contributed major advances, so a three-person cap leaves real credit disputes.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and industry programs, with the first clinical efficacy signals; the field is mature enough for recognition while still expanding rapidly.
uncertainties: Whether Ciulli (VHL ligands, rational design) or Sakamoto (first PROTAC) should displace one of the three.
Clinical approval of a PROTAC is still pending as far as I know; this is from memory and not verified.
The PROTAC and molecular-glue stories may be viewed as separate discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks and is a clear chemical-biology invention built on engineered deaminase chemistry. It opened precise genome correction, with clinical use and broad adoption across biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as trainee first authors on the cytosine and adenine editors. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were independent but contemporaneous. A Liu-only configuration is most defensible, though it risks sidelining co-inventors.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication and first clinical trials and patient treatments; timely, though the 2020 CRISPR chemistry prize makes the field's position debatable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B030) may split or defer recognition.
Whether the trainees or the Japanese group should share credit.
Long-term clinical safety data are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, a molecular-design solution for packaging and releasing nucleic acids in cells. Societal impact is enormous, and it fits well with chemistry that turns a discovery into a technology.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the early lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid concepts, with Hope and Madden as key co-inventors. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer made major contributions in optimization and development, so credit is widely distributed and arguably contested.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale by approved siRNA drugs and COVID-19 vaccines. Timing is strong, but the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA may lessen the appetite for a delivery-focused chemistry prize.
uncertainties: Attribution among Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved; my choice is from memory.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically and gave rise to long-read DNA/RNA sequencing and single-molecule analytics. It combines engineered protein pores, molecular recognition and instrumentation, and has spread widely across biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed nanopore sequencing, Kasianowicz showed single-stranded DNA translocation through alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered the pores and adapters, and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled reading. I selected Bayley, Deamer and Akeson, but a five-person field makes this contested.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and widely validated, with routine use in genomics and pathogen surveillance; more than mature enough.
uncertainties: Branton and possibly Bayley may be deceased, which would eliminate them from eligibility; I cannot verify this.
Sequencing may be viewed as primarily a biology or technology advance rather than chemistry.
Allocation of credit among five contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs let cells incorporate unnatural amino acids, giving chemists control over protein composition and function in living systems. It is a foundational tool for protein engineering, biophysics, biologics and bioorthogonal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first in vivo unnatural amino acid incorporation in bacteria and yeast, Wang did early work in his group, and Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes, multiple codons and genome recoding. Credit is plausibly a Schultz, Chin, Wang configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely used for two decades, with commercial applications such as site-specific antibody-drug conjugates; recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees Wang as a separate laureate from Schultz.
Overlap with bioorthogonal chemistry and phage-display themes of earlier prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures give nanometer-precise self-assembly and enable biosensing, nanophotonics and drug-carrier design. They embody the design-for-assembly principle that I care most about, with real reach into biotechnology.
assessment.attribution: Seeman founded structural DNA nanotechnology but is not on the list (and I believe he is deceased), so Rothemund's origami and the Yan and Yin groups' extension to complex structures are the practical alternatives. Winfree and Shih are also strong contributors. Credit assignment is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong, reproducible and widely adopted, yet translation to applications is still incomplete, so impact may be seen as partly prospective.
uncertainties: Absence of Seeman from the credited names.
Practical impact beyond a research tool is still emerging.
Which three of five is best is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid rise in solar cell efficiency from solution-processed materials and renewed thinking on defect-tolerant semiconductors. The work is chemically rich and strongly tied to energy materials.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells, Park and Snaith made the key efficiency and solid-state breakthroughs, and Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok were also decisive. A three-person limit forces difficult choices.
assessment.maturity: Intense independent confirmation and very rapid efficiency gains, but long-term stability and commercialization remain unresolved, which tempers timeliness.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity concerns may argue for waiting.
Credit among at least six candidates is contested.
Overlap with dye-sensitized cells (B015).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry measures intact noncovalent protein complexes, their stoichiometry and their ligand interactions, linking bioanalytical chemistry directly to structural biology and drug discovery. It changed what can be measured about assemblies that are hard to study otherwise.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck each made central, distinct contributions to technique, complexes and membrane proteins, giving a plausible three-person split. Loo and Gross are also credible.
assessment.maturity: Established and widely used, including for membrane proteins and in industry, though it is partly overshadowed by the 2002 mass spectrometry prize and by cryo-EM.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges it distinct enough from earlier mass spectrometry prizes.
Relative influence of Robinson, Heck and Chait is judged from memory.
